title: Shared atoms of the core-internal contract
description: Referenced by the other core-internal schemas; validates nothing on its own. Identifiers, amounts, timestamps, nodes and denominations are the provider-role contract's, and digests and names the module interface's, by reference.

token.description: A reason or a bound's name, as the component that gives it names it: a lower-case word or words joined by _.

count.description: A count of one or more, no larger than 2^53 - 1.

role.description: The role an actor acts in, each recorded apart even where one party holds several (REQ-AUD-8): a customer (requester, payer or beneficiary), the operator, a provider, a verifier, a regulator or a checker by an identified permission (REQ-AUZ-7), or one of Core's own parts acting on its own account. An agent acts in its party's role (REQ-OPS-5).

actor_kind.description: What kind of actor acts: a person, an agent acting for its accountable party within the scope that party set (REQ-AUZ-8), or a component (a module, a reserve's system, one of Core's parts). Humans and agents use one contract, and the record says which acted (REQ-OPS-5, REQ-ORD-10).

decided.description: A decision a later call carries out.

expires_at.description: When it ends, by Core's clock: after the request's at, and no later than its until.

actor.description: Who acts. Both identifiers are references, never an identity itself (REQ-AUD-6).

party.description: The accountable party it acts for: where limits bind and where actors are compared (REQ-AUZ-8, ADR-0011).

acts.description: The actor, as external authentication established it (REQ-AUZ-1).

when.description: When a verified entry's action happened, and by whose clock (REQ-AUD-1).

source.description: Whose clock gave the time (REQ-AUD-1): Core's own, or the module platform's as a record it handed over states it.

stated_when.description: When a party says it made a statement (REQ-AUD-1, REQ-AUD-2).

at.description: The time the maker states, its envelope's made_at.

source.description: Always the maker's own statement, which rutent has not verified.

reserve.description: The reserve: the provider of the route's last deposit.

node.description: The outer node it deposits to.

account.description: The account or address at the reserve, by reference; one the requester provides is part of the destination too (REQ-ORD-35).

route_end.description: What a route that moves value ends at, as the action states it, so policy can hold it against the authorisation (REQ-AUZ-3).

delivers.description: The amount it is expected to deliver, in the to asset's unit, to hold against any floor.

catalogue_change.description: A change to the catalogue, each a permission of its own (REQ-AUZ-6). accept_module, revoke_release, mark_stale, declare_exploited, reinstate, withdraw_release and promote are about one module release, and only they name its version; grant, revoke_grant and set_slippage are about one tuple, and only they name it. The Rust types check both.

action.description: An action policy decides: one that moves value, posts a route, changes the catalogue, moves a stuck order's value or erases a kept statement (REQ-AUZ-1, REQ-AUD-13).

action_move_value.description: Handing a segment's value-moving operation to its provider.

origin_reserve.description: The order's origin reserve: the provider of its first withdrawal, or the holding account's provider on a route handed on (REQ-AUZ-9).

route.description: What the route it belongs to ends at, as it stands now.

action_post_route.description: Posting a route, which only the operator may do (REQ-AUZ-2).

decision_record.description: The digest of the recorded decision that chose the route.

suggested_by.description: Who suggested it, if anyone did; a suggestion has no standing until posted (REQ-AUZ-2).

version.description: The module release it is about.

tuple.description: The tuple it is about, where it is about one.

advertising_keys.description: The provider's advertising keys, at least one, each once: named exactly by a grant, which the Rust types check. The latest grant in the log replaces them, and they are the log's first trust in the provider's advertisements.

statement_key.description: The key the release's module signs its statements with: named exactly by accept_module, which the Rust types check.

action_erase_statement.description: Erasing a kept statement's bytes from the evidence store, a decided action: the store erases only on its effect's done result, and the commitment stays in the log (REQ-AUD-13).

commitment.description: The commitment the bytes are kept under.

reason.description: Why, as a token: a label to read, which no decision branches on.

action_resolve_stuck.description: Moving a stuck order's value as its decide step named, outside the order's authorisation (REQ-AUZ-4, ADR-0011).

carries_out.description: The decide step's decision it carries out.

resolution.description: The outcome it moves, exactly as the decide step named it, the provider that moves it included; the log admits it only so.

transaction.description: The transaction the move goes under at that provider: what its outcome's evidence is about, as a move_value's is about its segment.

refusal_class.description: Why policy refused, as a stable class: the actor's role or permissions don't allow it; an input the decision needs is missing (REQ-AUZ-5); it isn't inside the authorisation it names (REQ-AUZ-3); the accountable party is past its bound (REQ-OPS-1, REQ-AUZ-8, REQ-CPL-5); the actor acts for no identified accountable party (REQ-AUZ-8); or one accountable party would both decide a stuck order's outcome and move its value (REQ-AUZ-4).

not_known_cause.description: Why policy could not decide (REQ-AUZ-5); nothing moves on it.
